title: Wilhelmina Barth, pianist on the jitney dance
summary: He describes Barth's piano style, size and touch, and what he knows of her later life.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I was going to ask a little bit more. Wait a minute. Can you tell us a little about Wilhelmina Barth? Because I never did get to hear her. I know she was a good pianist. What style did she play? What kind of piano?

Well, like I told you, Bill, on a Jitney dance, you see the styles varied. When she came to work early at night, she might have played like pad of whiskey, like you say. But as the hours started to go, she was finally wide up playing like stormy weather, you know, just sitting up there caught in the wind. Because as I told you, the man used to wake us like mules. Don't let the echo of the first piece die out before you pick up another one. That was the rules we had. What size lady? Was she big and strong? Oh, yeah. She was kind of hefty. Yeah. She was kind of on the portly side. She was pretty strong. Had a heavy touch. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Yeah. She had a very heavy hand. Yeah. She was a very good piano player. Did she teach music or read music and all of it? Well, yes. Yes. She read music. But as far as teaching it, I didn't know.
I heard that she's teaching now. Somebody talked like maybe she was teaching in late years.

Well, I wouldn't know. All I know is that she joined a church out there with another friend of mine. You remember that fellow I made you sell it right to Dr. Blanks? Oh, yeah. Yeah, well, she joined Dr. Blanks' church. That's on Bienville and Durban.
Does she live in town or across the lake or something?

Well, I don't know. I haven't seen her in quite a while. Last time I saw her when Percy's daughter. Percy's daughter got married. Oh, yeah. And we played up there that night, you see. And she was at the dance. I heard that too. Well, I haven't seen her since. Now, where she's at, I wouldn't know. But that's the last time I had an occasion to see her.
